author: Triage Nurse
note_text:
Pt presents c/o SOB + fever x4d, productive cough (green sputum). Appears unwell, tachypneic, using accessory muscles.
Obs:
- BP 135/80
- HR 105
- RR 24
- Temp 39.1
- SpO₂ 90% RA → ↑ to 94% on 2L NP
Reduced AE R base. Pt placed in monitored bed. MD notified.

author: ED Physician
note_text:
84M w/ 4d hx fever, productive cough, progressive dyspnea. No CP/hemoptysis.
PMH: AF (no anticoag), HTN, HLD
Meds: BB
Exam: Gen: febrile, tachypneic CV: irregularly irregular Resp: crackles + bronchial BS RLL, ↓ AE base
CXR: RLL consolidation
Impression: severe CAP
Plan: blood cultures, IV abx, O₂, admit

author: ED Nurse
note_text:
IV x2 inserted. Bloods + cultures sent. IV abx commenced.
Pt febrile, diaphoretic, frequent productive cough. Tolerating O₂.

author: Internal Medicine Physician
note_text:
Persistent fever (T max 38.8), ↑ WOB overnight. O₂ now 4L.
Exam: RR ~26, ongoing crackles RLL, fatigued appearance
Labs: ↑ inflammatory markers
Assessment: worsening pneumonia, ?early RF
Plan: escalate abx, close monitoring, consider ICU

author: ICU Physician
note_text:
Deterioration overnight → worsening hypoxia, tiring.
On arrival: RR >30, SpO₂ 88% high-flow
Intubated for hypoxic RF. Vent initiated (moderate settings). Hemodynamically stable.
Dx: severe necrotizing pneumonia

author: ICU Nurse
note_text:
Pt sedated, ventilated (FiO₂ ~50%). Thick purulent secretions on suction.
HR irregular. BP stable. UO adequate.

author: ICU Physician
note_text:
Limited improvement. High secretion burden.
Notable continuous bubbling in vent circuit → significant air leak.
Ventilation suboptimal (volume loss).
Concern: BPF → CT requested

author: Radiologist
note_text: RLL necrotizing consolidation w/ cavitation. Communication seen between bronchial tree + pleural space → consistent w/ BPF.

author: ICU Physician
note_text:
Persistent large air leak. Vent inefficiency, failed weaning attempts.
BPF likely cause.
Plan: pulmonary consult

author: Pulmonologist
note_text:
BPF secondary to necrotizing infection. Air leak significant → impairing ventilation + preventing weaning.
Plan: bronchoscopic closure attempt
- tetracycline instillation
- blood clot occlusion
Discussed w/ ICU team, NOK consent obtained.

author: Pulmonologist
note_text:
Flexible bronchoscopy via ETT.
Findings: fistula identified RLL segmental bronchus.
Intervention:
- tetracycline instilled locally
- autologous clot placed
No immediate complications.

author: ICU Nurse
note_text:
Stable post bronchoscopy.
Air leak markedly reduced. Tidal volumes improved. Monitoring ongoing.

author: ICU Physician
note_text:
Marked improvement. Air leak resolved. Gas exchange improved.
Plan: begin weaning.

author: ICU Physician
note_text:
Successfully extubated this AM.
Now on 2L NP O₂, comfortable. No evidence recurrent air leak.

author: ICU Nurse
note_text: Pt awake, oriented. Mild cough. No respiratory distress. SpO₂ >95% low-flow O₂.

author: Internal Medicine Physician
note_text:
Stepped down from ICU.
Breathing comfortably, crackles improving. No signs of air leak. Mobilizing slowly.

author: Physiotherapist
note_text: Deconditioned post ICU. Mobilizing w/ assistance. Stable RR. Breathing exercises initiated.

author: Ward Nurse
note_text: Pt improving. Ambulating short distances. Eating well. Afebrile. No SOB at rest.

author: Attending Physician
note_text:
84M w/ severe CAP → necrotizing pneumonia + RF requiring intubation.
Complicated by BPF → persistent air leak preventing ventilator weaning.
Treated with bronchoscopic tetracycline instillation + clot occlusion → successful closure.
Extubated Day 9, recovered well.
Discharge: stable, ambulatory, no air leak.
Follow-up: pulmonology

author: Pulmonologist
note_text:
Pt well. No dyspnea or cough. Imaging improving. No recurrence.
Assessment: resolved BPF post bronchoscopic management.
